name: Times club monthly special crossword No 20,264

solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Lean across hard, with gusto pushing forward a person without luck

indicators.note: lying across something means stretching round it, so one word wraps the other
pushing something forward changes its place in the line, so the letters of gusto get rearranged

blocks.note: lean means thin
H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard
gusto is eager enthusiasm

explanation.surface: Someone leans over hard and pushes eagerly ahead, yet is still unlucky.
explanation.walkthrough: SLIM goes across H to give SHLIM; ZEAL has its A pushed to the front to give AZEL. SHLIMAZEL is Yiddish.
explanation.definitionFit: A shlimazel is a chronically unfortunate person in Yiddish, a born loser to whom mishaps always happen.

clue.text: Stripper maybe taking fig leaf from statue, bra oddly chosen

indicators.note: oddly chosen means only the letters in odd positions are picked out of the words before it

blocks.note: first, third and fifth letters of statue
first and third letters of bra

explanation.surface: A statue loses its fig leaf in a risqué strip, with a bra thrown in.
explanation.walkthrough: The stripper is not a performer but an insect that strips leaves, so the fig leaf is literal foliage.
explanation.definitionFit: The sauba is a South American leaf-cutting ant that strips trees of their foliage, so it might carry off a fig leaf.

clue.text: Pound note Arthur’s dad has stopped sticking out window

indicators.note: to stop something is to plug a gap in it, so this name sits inside the other letters

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for a pound (libra)
Uther Pendragon was the father of King Arthur
n is the reference abbreviation for a note, as in a footnote

explanation.surface: A pound note has been used to plug a window that Arthur's father left jutting out.
explanation.walkthrough: UTHER plugs the gap between L and N.
explanation.definitionFit: A luthern is a dormer window, one that projects outward from a sloping roof.

clue.text: The boring Victorians in shock: what was corrupt about king?

indicators.note: something corrupt has been spoiled out of its proper form, so the letters of was are jumbled
about means surrounding, so the jumbled letters go round the royal abbreviation

blocks.note: a shock of hair is a mop
eh? is a way of saying what?
taken as written
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: Stuffy Victorians are shocked at the corrupt behaviour surrounding a king.
explanation.walkthrough: Victorians here are not Queen Victoria's subjects but people from the Australian state of Victoria, where the word was used.
explanation.definitionFit: Mopehawks is Australian slang for dull, tedious people, the bores of that region.

clue.text: Exercise with music mostly that is up on pitch for one at Bayern

indicators.note: mostly means most but not all, so the last letter of the fitness class is dropped
in a down clue, up means the letters are read from bottom to top

blocks.note: Zumba is a dance-fitness workout done to music
i.e. is the abbreviation for id est, that is
a sales pitch is a spiel

explanation.surface: A music-backed workout session gets ready to start on a football pitch in Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: Bayern is Bavaria in German, so the definition asks for German: 'for one' means 'for example'.
explanation.definitionFit: Zum Beispiel is the German phrase meaning for example, which is what 'for one' means in English.

clue.text: A huge amount on the subcontinent raised, not all collected

definitions.text: A huge amount on the subcontinent

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means lifted so the letters read upward
not all of a word means its final letter is cut off

blocks.note: a collected person is composed and calm

explanation.surface: A vast sum is raised in India, but not all of it is collected.
explanation.walkthrough: CALM loses its last letter to CAL, which is then read upward.
explanation.definitionFit: A lac or lakh is the Indian unit for one hundred thousand, typically of rupees, so a huge amount.

clue.text: Seafood to take all for oneself and others?

blocks.note: Co is the abbreviation for company, as in '& Co'
to hog is to keep everything for yourself

explanation.surface: Someone greedy grabs all the seafood, then wonders about the others.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces appear in reverse order in the clue: the CO for 'and others' comes first in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Cohog is a variant spelling of quahog, an edible hard-shelled clam from the North American Atlantic coast.

clue.text: Tea in the afternoon after picking up food in Dungannon

indicators.note: in a down clue, picking up means lifting the letters so they read upward

blocks.note: cha is a slang word for tea
p.m. marks times in the afternoon

explanation.surface: Afternoon tea is served after collecting some food in a Northern Irish town.
explanation.walkthrough: Dungannon is a town in Northern Ireland, where champ is a staple dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Champ is an Irish dish of mashed potatoes beaten with spring onions, milk and butter.

clue.text: Approval American got in greeting Japanese artist

indicators.note: got in means placed inside, so the first two pieces sit within the salutation

blocks.note: hi is a greeting
OK signals approval
USA stands for American, United States of America

explanation.surface: An American gives an approving nod while greeting a Japanese painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Hokusai was the Japanese printmaker famous for The Great Wave off Kanagawa woodblock print.

clue.text: One not, however, made of the right stuff for holding punch

definitions.text: One not, however, made of the right stuff for holding punch

blocks.clueFragment: made of the right stuff for holding punch
blocks.note: surface reading: a vessel that ought to be good for serving the drink punch
setter's reading: a fragile jaw that cannot hold up against a blow, despite being made of the stuff drinking vessels are

explanation.walkthrough: Punch is both a drink and a blow; glass is ideal for holding the first and hopeless for taking the second.
explanation.definitionFit: A boxer with a glass chin is easily knocked out, the jaw being too fragile to absorb blows.

clue.text: Pancake with a little butter in initially might tempt you back

indicators.note: initially means only the opening letters of the following words count
in places the butter piece inside the string of opening letters
back means the whole sequence is read from end to start

blocks.note: first letter of might
taken as written
a pat is a small portion of butter
first letter of tempt
U is text-speak for you

explanation.surface: A pancake with a dab of butter might tempt you to return for more.
explanation.walkthrough: A PAT goes inside M, T, U to give MAPATTU, which read backwards is UTTAPAM.
explanation.definitionFit: Uttapam is a thick South Indian pancake made from fermented rice and lentil batter with toppings.

clue.text: Hear that Switzerland has secured ace Indian spinner

indicators.note: securing something means holding it fast, so the country code wraps round the call to listen

blocks.note: CH is the international vehicle code for Switzerland
hark! means listen to that
A is the abbreviation for ace on playing cards

explanation.surface: Listen up: the Swiss have signed a top-class Indian spin bowler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spinner' suggests a cricket bowler, but this spinner spins thread.
explanation.definitionFit: A charkha is the traditional Indian spinning wheel, famously used by Gandhi for homespun cotton.

clue.text: Stop representing The Ox’s Head pub after drink there?

indicators.note: after places the pub abbreviation behind the word for a beer

blocks.note: ale is a drink
PH is the map abbreviation for public house

explanation.surface: Calling last orders at The Ox's Head pub after a drink there.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ox's Head looks like a pub name, but it describes the Hebrew letter, whose early form was a drawing of an ox's head and which stands for a glottal stop.
explanation.definitionFit: Aleph, first Hebrew letter, represents a glottal stop and derives from a pictograph of an ox's head.

clue.text: Ditches customs after wish for peace in rest of much of Europe?

indicators.note: after places the word for habits behind the other two pieces

blocks.note: the EU, European Union, covers most of Europe
RIP stands for requiescat in pace, rest in peace
uses are customs or habitual practices

explanation.surface: Europe drops its customs controls after a hope for peace across the continent.
explanation.definitionFit: A euripus is a strait or channel with a strong current, so the plural can stand for ditches or channels.

clue.text: One way to render adept and voluble, but shallow?

indicators.note: to render a word is to make it into something else, here by shaking its letters about

blocks.note: rattling is one way of shaking letters into a new order
taken as written, then shaken up

explanation.surface: A question of whether being adept and talkative might hide a lack of depth.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer describes its own making: RATTLE the letters of ADEPT and you get PATED.
explanation.definitionFit: Rattle-pated means empty-headed and chattering, someone talkative with little in the head.

clue.text: Local has to chew on chestnut leaves

indicators.note: leaves means departs, so the abbreviation walks out of the word for chewing

blocks.note: to munch is to chew
ch is the dictionary abbreviation for chestnut, the horse colour

explanation.surface: A villager must chew chestnut leaves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' looks like foliage on the tree, but it is a verb: CH leaves MUNCH.
explanation.definitionFit: Mun is a dialect form of must, so a local speaker would say it for has to.

clue.text: Commentaries shedding little light, on reflection not considered the writer’s

indicators.note: a reflection shows things mirror-wise, so the word for faint is read backwards

blocks.note: something dim gives off little light
a rash act is one not considered beforehand
the writer is I, and the writer's (the writer is) gives I'M

explanation.surface: A writer reflects that some commentaries shed little light and were not well thought out.
explanation.definitionFit: Midrashim are rabbinic interpretations and expositions of Hebrew scripture.

clue.text: Gifts for woodcutter, one going for high speed burrowing rodent

indicators.note: one going for another means one of a set is taken out and something else takes its place

blocks.note: in the folk tale the woodcutter is granted three wishes
a ton is slang for a hundred miles an hour

explanation.surface: A fairy's gifts to a woodcutter include a speedy creature that digs underground.
explanation.walkthrough: Of the three wishes, the middle one is swapped for TON.
explanation.definitionFit: Wishtonwish is an old name for the prairie dog, a North American ground squirrel living in burrows.

clue.text: Swimmers looking skyward? A complete absence of air cadets doing that

indicators.note: doing that means looking skyward, and in a down clue that sends the letters upward

blocks.note: not one means none at all
ATC is the Air Training Corps, the UK air cadets

explanation.surface: Nobody in the air cadets is swimming on their back gazing at the sky.
explanation.walkthrough: The Air Training Corps is the British youth organisation for air cadets.
explanation.definitionFit: Notonecta is the genus of backswimmers, water bugs that swim upside down with their bellies facing the sky.

clue.text: Move ladies especially with ultimate in scent? I might have

definitions.text: Move ladies especially with ultimate in scent? I might have

indicators.note: especially hints at something made specially, so the letters before it are arranged anew
ultimate means last, so only the final letter of the word is kept

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
last letter of scent

explanation.surface: A flower boasts it might be the scent that moves ladies most.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines the answer: a fragrant flower might move ladies with its scent.
explanation.definitionFit: Dame's-violet, or sweet rocket, is a garden plant prized for its strong evening fragrance that might charm women.

clue.text: Compound with alternative arrangement to time-share did come across duller

indicators.note: two pieces sharing a time letter means it is written only once where they meet

blocks.note: to meet is to come across someone
tamer means less exciting

explanation.surface: A timeshare deal is rearranged when the buyer meets a duller alternative.
explanation.walkthrough: T stands for time; MET ends and TAMER begins with it, so the two words share one T.
explanation.definitionFit: A metamer is a compound with the same molecular formula as another but a different structural arrangement of atoms.

clue.text: Maybe a red coverlet civil servants all have

blocks.note: read cryptically, each of the words coverlet

explanation.surface: A red bedspread is standard issue for every civil servant.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay is a statement about spelling: coverlet, civil and servants all have V in, and V IN is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Vin is French for wine, and a red is one example of wine, hence the 'Maybe'.

clue.text: Observe and say nothing: one’s not Indian

blocks.note: vide is Latin for see, used in references
sh! is a call for silence
I is the Roman numeral one; the 's means one is

explanation.surface: Someone told to watch quietly confesses they are not from India.
explanation.definitionFit: Videshi is a Hindi word for foreign, describing goods or people from outside India.

clue.text: Milking applause perhaps for surprising sequel

blocks.note: first meaning, read in two parts: a performer milking applause is after more clapping
second meaning: an unexpected later consequence

explanation.surface: A performer milks the applause and is rewarded with an unexpected encore.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half splits the answer into its two words, a cryptic reading rather than a dictionary meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: An afterclap is an unexpected event or consequence following something supposedly over.

clue.text: Plenty of Scots left in cold? Consistently the reverse

indicators.note: the reverse applied consistently means each word is swapped for its opposite

blocks.note: the opposite of left is right, R
the opposite of in is out
the opposite of cold is hot, H on a tap

explanation.surface: Abundant Scots are left out in the cold, or is it the other way round?
explanation.walkthrough: Every word of 'left in cold' is swapped for its opposite: right, out, hot.
explanation.definitionFit: Routh is a regional Scottish noun meaning abundance, so a great quantity of something counts.

clue.text: Girl from the right charity, Centre for Change

indicators.note: centre for means only the middle letters of the next word are taken
reading from the right means reading backwards

blocks.note: aid is charitable help
the middle two letters of change

explanation.surface: A girl comes from the right charity, the Centre for Change.
explanation.definitionFit: Nadia is a female first name.

clue.text: It’s unladylike to hide up trees

indicators.note: to hide means the letters are concealed within the words before
in a down clue, up means the letters read from bottom to top

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of it's and the start of unladylike

explanation.surface: A lady is told that hiding up a tree is unbecoming.
explanation.definitionFit: Alnus is the botanical genus of alder trees.

clue.text: May bug university doctor with endless joyful call to nurse

indicators.note: endless means the final letter is cut off the cheer
to nurse is to hold close, so the cheer cradles the other pieces

blocks.note: U is the abbreviation for university
MB is a medical degree, Bachelor of Medicine
huzza is a cheer of joy

explanation.surface: A university doctor might bug a patient with a cheery call to the nurse.
explanation.walkthrough: May bug is the cockchafer beetle, not a request to pester; the cheer goes round the two abbreviations just after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Humbuzz is a dialect name for the cockchafer, a large beetle also called the maybug.

clue.text: What may be represented by cipher or code

definitions.text: What may be represented by cipher

blocks.clueFragment: What may be represented by cipher
blocks.note: first meaning: a cipher is a zero, which stands for nothing at all
second meaning: the American postal code

explanation.walkthrough: Cipher looks like secret writing alongside code, but here it means the figure nought. A zip code is the US postcode.
explanation.definitionFit: Zip is slang for nothing, which a zero represents, and the ZIP code is the American postal code system.

clue.text: Food’s at home and gives a comfortable retirement?

blocks.note: tuck is British slang for food, especially sweets at school; with the 's
in means at home

explanation.surface: Someone with food in the house enjoys a cosy retirement.
explanation.walkthrough: Retirement here means going to bed, not giving up work.
explanation.definitionFit: To tuck someone in is to settle them snugly in bed, making their retiring for the night comfortable.

clue.text: Bitterness of NZ writer when another article comes in for slating at first

indicators.note: at first means only the opening letter of the word is taken
comes in for means takes the place of, as a substitute does

blocks.note: Ngaio Marsh was a New Zealand crime novelist
a is the indefinite article
first letter of slating

explanation.surface: A New Zealand writer feels bitter when another article about her gets a slating.
explanation.walkthrough: In MARSH, A replaces S.
explanation.definitionFit: Marah is a Hebrew word for bitterness, the name of a bitter spring in Exodus.

clue.text: Page head for paper with large sign: “Jobs for Sellers”

blocks.note: p is the abbreviation for page
the editor heads a newspaper
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
Aries is a sign of the zodiac

explanation.surface: A newspaper editor runs a big headline advertising jobs for salespeople.
explanation.definitionFit: Pedlaries are the trade or wares of a pedlar, the work of travelling hawkers.
